title: An `await` result is typed as a shape and built as a class named `Core\Script\Result`, so it renders and encodes as a class.
text: `crates/nvs-types/src/expr/isolate.rs:51` types the result of `await` as a `rule:types/shape-type` shape, and `rule:types/anonymous-object` makes such a value an ordinary object of a compiler-synthesized class, which `Core\Debug::render` prints as `$shape{ok,value}#1` and `Core\Json::encode` writes as a JSON object (`tests/conformance/core/json-encodes-a-shape-as-an-object.nvst`). The result of `await spawn script` renders as `Core\Script\Result#1`, a class name no program can write, and `Core\Json::encode` of it throws `LogicError`: an instance of `Core\Script\Result` has no JSON encoding. `SHAPE_ROSTER` names the three `Core` shape descriptors `Core\Issue`, `Core\Script\Result` and `Core\Script\Failure` (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/instance.rs:652`, the names at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/script.rs:476` and `:482`), and `ClassDesc::is_shape` knows a shape only by the `$shape{` label (`crates/nvs-runtime/src/object.rs:1399`), so these values are classes to every reader of that test. Whether a `Core\Issue` inside a `ParseError` renders and encodes the same way is not checked. Closing it means each roster entry takes the label `nvs_ir::lower::shape_class_label` mints for its sorted field names, so render shows `$shape{error,ok,output,value}#1` and the encoder writes an object, with a case for each.
